## Summary

Adds `compare --systems native,baseline,candidate` so a run can choose which writer systems take part. The default is still all three. `baseline` and `candidate` are required, and full system names or the provider's native name are accepted.

Without `native`, no native writers run and only candidate vs baseline is judged (in both orders). Planned counts, rebuild coverage, the quality gate and `--plan` output follow the selected systems. A subset is recorded in the manifest settings, so it becomes part of the experiment identity. Runs with all three systems keep their previous identity. Resuming without `--systems` keeps the frozen systems.

The accuracy view's candidate-vs-baseline table also gains a composite delta, with a case-clustered 95% bootstrap interval computed from per-case means.

## Testing


Tests were added in `tests/comparison.test.ts` and `tests/score.test.ts`. No test results are claimed in this description.

title: Add compare --systems to choose writer systems; cross-model composite delta in score
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Tuning the graph candidate against the baseline needs runs that skip the native writers, and the score report needs a composite delta for candidate vs baseline across models.

`compare --systems native,baseline,candidate` now picks the writer systems; the default is all three, baseline and candidate are required, and both full names and the provider's native name are accepted. `selectSystems`/`manifestSystems` in `src/run/provider.ts` resolve the list, returning the provider's systems when none is given. An unrecognized name throws `Unknown system <name>`. Previously the comparison loop was fixed to `["tracetoon-baseline", provider.native]`; it now iterates the selected comparisons.

Without native, no native writers run and only candidate vs baseline is judged, in both orders. Planned counts, rebuild coverage, the quality gate and `--plan` output follow the selection; `--plan` gains `systems` and `judgedAgainst` keys. A subset is recorded in manifest settings and so in the experiment identity; runs with all three keep their previous identity. A resume without `--systems` keeps the frozen systems.

In `accuracyMarkdown` (`src/report/score.ts`), the candidate-vs-baseline table gains a composite delta with a case-clustered 95% bootstrap interval from per-case means; with a single shared case the interval prints as "–".

Tests were updated in `tests/comparison.test.ts` (restore, fakeComparisonSetup) and `tests/score.test.ts` (write, j). They cover the subset run, resume, and the clustered delta; the comparison tests use a fake setup, so they exercise the surrounding code rather than the real comparison setup.

Where to start: `compareV2` in `src/comparison.ts`.

Feedback wanted: resuming a subset run with all three systems is currently rejected; is that the right behavior?
